description.text: Michael Servetus was a Spanish theologian, physician, cartographer, and Renaissance humanist who became famous for his anti‑trinitarian writings and his pioneering description of pulmonary circulation. He was a polymath versed in many sciences—mathematics, astronomy, meteorology, geography, anatomy, medicine, pharmacology, jurisprudence, translation, poetry, and biblical studies—making him a key figure in the intellectual currents of the Reformation.

Born in 1511 (approximate) in Villanueva de Sigena, Aragon, Servetus died on 27 October 1553 in Geneva, where he was burned at the stake for heresy. His 1553 work *Christianismi Restitutio* contained the first European description of pulmonary circulation, and his radical theology sparked intense conflict with John Calvin and the Geneva council, marking a pivotal moment in the emergence of religious tolerance.

curiosities.text: He was the first European to correctly describe the function of pulmonary circulation.
He was executed by burning at stake in Geneva on 27 October 1553.
He was a polymath who wrote on mathematics, astronomy, meteorology, geography, anatomy, medicine, pharmacology, jurisprudence, translation, poetry, and biblical studies.
